wrong: sister/noun oewn-10621666-n: Extending a kin word to a fellow member claims warmth and solidarity that the plain 'member' or 'colleague' does not; a learner should know it lands as affectionate belonging.

mother/noun oewn-10352666-n: Addressing an unrelated old woman as 'mother' rather than 'madam' presumes a homely familiarity that marks her as old and humble, affectionate at best and patronising at worst.

lady/noun oewn-10262834-n: Chosen over the plain 'woman', 'lady' signals courtesy, deference and an assumption of gentility (the gloss itself says 'polite'), and in modern use can land as dated or patronising, so a learner needs to know how it lands.
